title: Connected families of homomorphisms between diagonalizable groups are constant
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $D_1,D_2$ be affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that for $i=1,2$ there is a finitely generated abelian group $M_i$ and an isomorphism $D_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F[M_i]$ of group schemes, where $F[M_i]$ has basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_{m'}=e_{m+m'}$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and inverse $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Let $X$ be a connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $F$, with its structure morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $x_0:\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ be an $F$-point. Write $X(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_F(\operatorname{Spec}A,X)$ for a commutative $F$-algebra $A$. Let $\phi:X\times_F D_1\to D_2$ be an $F$-morphism such that for every such $A$ and every $x\in X(A)$ the map $d\mapsto\phi(x,d)$ is a group homomorphism $D_1(A)\to D_2(A)$, naturally under change of $A$. Put $\phi_{x_0}(d)=\phi(x_{0,A},d)$, where $x_{0,A}$ is the base change of $x_0$. Then $\phi=\phi_{x_0}\circ\operatorname{pr}_{D_1}$ as $F$-morphisms. No smoothness or reducedness is required of $X,D_1,D_2$.

source.place: Theorem 12.36, printed pp.243--244, restricted to an algebraically closed field and an affine connected parameter scheme. The statement and the proof explicitly test all algebra-valued points, including nonreduced schemes.

proof.text: Choose the given group-scheme identifications and write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The point $x_0$ gives an $F$-algebra map $b_0:B\to F$, so $B\ne0$. By the affine fibre-product comparison [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $X\times_FD_1\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_FF[M_1])$, the projections being $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $e_m\mapsto1\otimes e_m$; so by the spectrum correspondence and the tensor-product universal property a pair $(x,d)\in X(A)\times D_1(A)$ is the algebra map $b\otimes e_m\mapsto x(b)d(e_m)$. Identify this algebra with $B[M_1]$ by $b\otimes e_m\mapsto be_m$: its inverse sends a finite sum $\sum b_me_m$ to $\sum b_m\otimes e_m$. Both maps preserve products and are inverse on the displayed generators. Thus $\phi$ gives an $F$-algebra map $f:F[M_2]\to B[M_1]$. Fix $n\in M_2$ and write $f(e_n)=u_n=\sum_m a_{n,m}e_m$, a finite sum. In the hypothesis take $A=B[M_1\oplus M_1]$, the point $x$ induced by $B\to A$, and the two points of $D_1$ induced by $e_m\mapsto e_{(m,0)}$ and $e_m\mapsto e_{(0,m)}$. Multiplicativity of $d\mapsto\phi(x,d)$, evaluated on $e_n$, gives $\sum_m a_{n,m}e_{(m,m)}=\sum_{m,l}a_{n,m}a_{n,l}e_{(m,l)}$. Taking instead $A=B$, the point induced by $1_B$ and the identity of $D_1(B)$, preservation of the identity gives $\sum_m a_{n,m}=1$. These are tests on all algebra-valued points, without passing to reduced schemes.

source.place: Theorem 12.36, pp.243--244; Remark 12.43, p.245, coordinate-ring interpretation (expanded).

proof.text: Compare the coefficients of the formal basis $e_{(m,l)}$ in the preceding equality. For $m=l$ one gets $a_{n,m}^2=a_{n,m}$; for $m\ne l$ one gets $a_{n,m}a_{n,l}=0$. This comparison is valid over any commutative ring: $B[M_1\oplus M_1]$ consists by definition of finitely supported functions to $B$, so equality is coefficientwise. Consequently the finitely many nonzero coefficients of each $u_n$ are pairwise orthogonal idempotents whose sum is $1$.

source.place: Remark 12.43, p.245: argument with basis monomials and a ring with no nontrivial idempotents (expanded coefficient calculation).

proof.text: Apply the connectedness criterion to the nonempty scheme $X$: every idempotent in $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is $0$ or $1$. For each fixed $n$, at least one coefficient $a_{n,m}$ is nonzero, since their finite sum is $1\ne0$, and every nonzero coefficient is therefore $1$. There cannot be two: their product would be $1$ by their values and $0$ by orthogonality. Thus for a unique $h(n)\in M_1$ we have $u_n=e_{h(n)}$, with coefficient $1_B$. No integral-domain assumption on $B$ has been used.

source.place: Remark 12.43, p.245, no nontrivial idempotents; Stacks Tag 0BUG, varieties.tex, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections, proof of (2), for the connectedness criterion.

proof.text: Pulling back along $x_0\times1_{D_1}$ applies $b_0$ to the coefficients of $f$. Since each $f(e_n)=e_{h(n)}$ has coefficient $1_B$, it becomes $e_{h(n)}\in F[M_1]$. Pulling this map back along $\operatorname{pr}_{D_1}$ includes the coefficients $F\to B$ and again gives $e_{h(n)}\in B[M_1]$. Hence $\phi$ and $\phi_{x_0}\circ\operatorname{pr}_{D_1}$ induce equal algebra maps on every $e_n$ and on $F$, and therefore on every finite sum. The uniqueness clause of the spectrum correspondence gives equality of the two morphisms, including on nonreduced test algebras.
